title: What Is Pressure?
hook: Pressure is force spread over an area. Concentrate the same push on a tiny spot and it skyrockets — which is why a sharp knife cuts and a thumbtack pierces.
key_points: Pressure equals force divided by the area it acts on.
Same force on a smaller area means more pressure — knives, needles, and tacks.
Spreading force over a large area lowers pressure — snowshoes and skis.
In a fluid, pressure pushes equally in all directions and grows with depth.
content_html: Pressure is how much force is pressing on each bit of area — literally force divided by area. That's why what matters isn't just how hard you push, but how concentrated the push is. Press your palm against a table and nothing happens; press a thumbtack with the same force and the point sinks in, because all that force is funneled into a tiny tip.
extra_html: The flip side is just as useful: spread a force over a big area and the pressure drops. Snowshoes and skis let you cross snow that would otherwise swallow your boots, simply by enlarging the contact area. In fluids, pressure works a little differently — it pushes outward equally in every direction, and it climbs the deeper you go, which is why your ears ache at the bottom of a pool. Wikipedia's article on pressure lays out the definition and these everyday consequences.

related.title: Atmospheric Pressure
related.hook: Air has weight, and the whole column of it above you presses down — about 101 kPa at sea level. That push is what makes straws and suction cups work.

related.title: Buoyancy: Why Things Float
related.hook: Any fluid pushes up on what's in it with a force equal to the weight of fluid it shoves aside. Match your weight that way and you float — that's Archimedes.

flashcards.prompt: How is pressure related to force and area?
flashcards.back_html: Pressure is force divided by area. The same force on a smaller area produces a much higher pressure.

flashcards.prompt: Why do wide snowshoes keep you from sinking into snow?

choices.text: They spread your weight over a larger area, lowering the pressure
They warm the snow so it holds firm

flashcards.explanation_html: Spreading the same weight (force) over more area reduces the pressure on the snow, so you don't punch through.

flashcards.prompt: How does pressure behave inside a fluid?

choices.text: It pushes equally in all directions and increases with depth
It only pushes downward, like gravity
It is the same at every depth

flashcards.explanation_html: Fluid pressure acts in all directions at once, and the weight of fluid above means deeper points feel more pressure.
